title: Sikhs in science
hook: Sikh scientists and doctors have served worldwide, like Narinder Singh Kapany in fiber optics

segments.voice: Yesterday, Milkha Singh, and your line was from orphan to athlete. Today, something even faster than a sprinter: light.

Under the street outside, or under the ocean, a pulse of light is racing along a strand of glass thinner than a hair. It bends around corners and follows the cable down hills and across seabeds. Your last video call, the photo you sent this morning: there's a fair chance some of it traveled as light inside glass. Long before anyone streamed anything, a young Sikh physicist was asking a simple question. Can light be made to go around a bend? Today: Sikhs in science.
screen: `LIGHT RACING THROUGH GLASS.` → `AROUND CORNERS, UNDER OCEANS.` → `CAN LIGHT GO AROUND A BEND?`

segments.voice: First, the question. Light, as school science teaches, travels in straight lines. Narinder Singh Kapany, a physicist from Punjab, worked with others on bundles of very thin glass fibers that could carry light, and even an image, along a curved path. He wrote about the work under a plain name: fiber optics. Second, how it works. Inside a clear glass fiber, light hits the wall at a shallow angle and bounces back in, again and again, so it stays trapped and follows the fiber wherever it bends. Physicists call it total internal reflection. The light doesn't go around the corner so much as ricochet around it. Third, the wider picture. Kapany is one Sikh name in science; other Sikhs have worked as scientists, engineers and doctors, in Punjab and far from it. He also gave his time and money to Sikh art and Sikh studies, and wore the turban. Science and the Sikh story sat in the same life without a fight. Fourth, the root. At Ang 1349 of the Guru Granth Sahib, in a hymn of Bhagat Kabir, the whole world wells up from one light. Gurbani talks often about jot, the divine light in every being. A physicist studies how light moves through glass; a Sikh hears of one light moving through every life. Those are different kinds of claim, and nobody needs to blend them. But both start by paying attention to light.
screen: `CAN LIGHT GO AROUND A BEND?` · `IT BOUNCES BACK IN, AGAIN AND AGAIN.` · `SCIENTISTS, DOCTORS, ENGINEERS.` · `THE WORLD WELLS UP FROM ONE LIGHT.` · then, large: `LIGHT IN GLASS.`

segments.voice: Sit facing a window or a lamp, look at the light for one breath, then close your eyes and notice the glow that stays behind your eyelids. Let your attention rest on that faint brightness for a while. If you pray, you can say Waheguru and hold the thought of one light in every being.
Fiber optics. The work of Narinder Singh Kapany and others, carrying light, and even an image, through bent glass fibers. Today's word.
Your line: light in glass. One kind studied, one kind sung. Day one thousand twenty, complete.
